labs.name: NMED free well-water screening (field offices and water fairs; not a certified lab test)
labs.address: Statewide: drop off at an NMED field office, or bring a sample to a water fair
accredited_for: Not on the certified list (NMED screening). Field offices: nitrate, iron, fluoride
Water fairs: arsenic, electrical conductivity, fluoride, iron, nitrate, pH, sulfate
labs.detail: Phone is NMED's Ground Water Quality Bureau, which runs the water fairs (gwqb.general@env.nm.gov).
labs.note: NMED's Free Well Water Testing page says it tests private domestic wells free "only for Nitrate, Iron and Fluoride": collect at least one quart from the kitchen cold tap in a clean covered container, fill out the Well Testing Form, and bring both to your nearest NMED field office; results come by mail. NMED's Ground Water Quality Bureau also holds water fairs (the Private Wells page says eight a year) that test arsenic, electrical conductivity, fluoride, iron, nitrate, pH and sulfate, with results mailed in 2-4 weeks; dates are on the NMED events calendar. NMED says these are screenings only and do not replace certified lab testing. Neither tests for bacteria.
labs.source_name: NMED: Free Well Water Testing (page prints no date; fetched 2026-11-18)
labs.source_name_2: NMED Ground Water Quality Bureau: Water Fairs page (fetched 2026-11-18)

labs.name: BSN dba Indepth Water Testing
labs.detail: NMED certification number NM9412; analyte groups as printed: "M"; certification expires 4/16/2028; on contract with NMED-DWB: yes.
labs.source_name: NMED Drinking Water Bureau: Laboratories Certified by NMED-DWB to Analyze Drinking Water Samples (PDF, last updated 10/26/2026)
labs.note: Indepth's own site says it has tested water "for public water systems and well owners in Santa Fe and northern New Mexico since 1986" and lists "Homeowner Wells". Posted prices (tax not included): coliform and E. coli $80; bacteria and nitrate $130 (2-3 business days); bacteria, nitrate and lead (FHA/VA) $280 (10-14 business days); a 32-element panel that includes arsenic, fluoride, lead, manganese, nitrate and uranium $495 (14-17 business days). Bacteria samples must reach the lab within 24 hours of collection, kept cold; samples dropped off after 3:00 pm Thursday or on Friday add a $100 fee. Payment is due at drop-off; sampling visits are charged by time and mileage. Note NMED certifies this lab for microbiology only, so the chemistry in its panels is not covered by the NMED certification shown here; ask who runs those tests. The site gives (505) 473-7973 and the address above; NMED prints (505) 471-2023.
